tone_statements.citation: Leenhardt, Maurice. 1946. Langues et dialectes de l'Austro-Mélanésie. Paris: Institut d'Ethnologie.
tone_statements.quote: 6. — NEKU. Aire. — Bourail, Ouaoué, Goaro; Moindou, Moméa. 150 indigènes. I PHONÉTIQUE. § 1. — Transcription. Mêmes consonnes et voyelles, et même valeur, qu'en BOEWE. § 2. — Accent et ton. âre¹ = nous, bas. âre³ = ils, haut. II MOTS. § 3. — Tous les mots se terminent par une voyelle. [p. 11, end of the general Phonétique chapter:] Il reste à connaître l'accent, le ton, et les particularités phonétiques de chaque langue. On en trouvera le détail au chapitre réservé à chacune de celles-ci.
tone_statements.translation: 6. NEKU. Area: Bourail, Ouaoué, Goaro; Moindou, Moméa. 150 natives. I. Phonetics. §1 Transcription: same consonants and vowels, with the same values, as in Boewe [Orowe]. §2 Accent and tone: âre¹ = 'we', low; âre³ = 'they', high. II. Words. §3 All words end in a vowel. [p. 11:] It remains to establish the accent, the tone and the phonetic particularities of each language; the details are given in the chapter devoted to each.
tone_statements.locator: p. 43, Première partie III.6 Neku, §§1-2; and p. 11, II. Phonétique, closing paragraph
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 pitch levels noted (bas ¹ / haut ³) on one pronoun pair

tone.says: Not read in this task (record and secondary citation only). It is the classic areal/historical phonology survey of New Caledonia by the author of the NC tonogenesis hypothesis, giving phoneme inventories by language group and identifying the tone languages of the Centre (Paicî, Cèmuhî) and Far South; whether it states explicitly that the Bourail language ('Ôrôê) lacks tone was not verified.

tone.says: The Neku notice has a two-line paragraph '§ 2. Accent et ton' giving one pitch-distinguished pair in Leenhardt's superscript tone-number notation — âre¹ 'nous' marked bas (low) vs âre³ 'ils' marked haut (high); nothing further on tone or accent in the notice (transcription otherwise 'as in Boewe'); the general Phonétique chapter (p. 11) defers 'l'accent, le ton' to each language's notice. Earliest (impressionistic) report of a pitch contrast in Neku; no tone inventory or analysis.
